 Pete Buttigieg says Democrats went too far on student loans
 Monday, 16 November 2026, 04:22 
 Photo source: Fox News 
 He said college should be more affordable and students should be able to graduate debt-free, but rejected a universal fix for existing borrowers. 
 Former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg said in a Sunday interview that Democrats had “overtorqued” the student-loan issue and may have dissuaded voters. Host Dan Pfeiffer said many Democratic candidates who won in the midterm elections disagreed with the party on at least one issue, such as gun control or the role of oil and gas in energy, and asked Buttigieg which of his views differed from the party mainstream.
 This is reported by Fox News .
 In the 2020 campaign, I definitely staked out some positions that I still believe in that weren't always kind of popular in the party. One thing is, I think...we really overtorqued on the student loan thing. As a party, I have a very hard time explaining to my relatives in Michigan who did not go to college why they should be paying for people who do. 
 - Pete Buttigieg
 I believe there are ways to make sure that you come out of college debt-free. I believe college should be more affordable. I don't believe in like a magic wand to fix that for everybody who borrowed money. 
 - Pete Buttigieg
 Buttigieg previously served under President Joe Biden, who repeatedly attempted to cancel student-loan debt, even after the Supreme Court ruled against his administration in 2023. Buttigieg's husband, Chasten Buttigieg, was also among those frustrated at the prospect of making student-loan payments after COVID-19-era relief was set to expire in 2022. Fox News Digital said it reached out to Buttigieg's organization, Win the Era, for comment.
 Advertisement 
 Democratic strategist Julian Epstein called student-loan forgiveness a scam and congratulated Buttigieg for acknowledging that, saying he showed unusual self-awareness for a Democratic elite on the issue.
 The student loan giveaway, also known as loan forgiveness, is a scam. It's welfare for the most privileged and elite amongst us that the working class has to help fund. It's Robin Hood in reverse, and it stands against everything the Democratic Party should be standing for. 
 - Julian Epstein
 Buttigieg also said he disagreed with the Democratic Party on the two-party system.
 That makes some Democratic organizations nervous when you talk that way, but I think that a lot of the problems we've had around polarization, gerrymandering, even some of what goes on with money would be better if we were actually a healthy multi-party democracy. 
 - Pete Buttigieg
